answers.stem_only: Snapshots encrypted with the AWS managed key for EBS cannot be shared, and that key's policy cannot be edited. Copy each snapshot re-encrypted with a customer managed key, grant only the backup account use of that key, share the copies with only that account, and have the backup account copy them again with a KMS key it owns, so its copies no longer depend on any production-account key.

Use EBS Multi-Attach, which is available only on Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2) volumes on Nitro instances in the same AZ, and put a cluster-aware file system (for example GFS2 or OCFS2) on the volume so the cluster software coordinates concurrent writes; a standard file system such as XFS or ext4 would corrupt data, and writing custom block-level coordination is high overhead.

Large sequential reads with a sustained throughput need on a multi-TiB volume point to Throughput Optimized HDD (st1): its baseline throughput scales with size, so a 2 TiB st1 volume has a baseline above 60 MiB/s at a lower price per GB than gp3. Cold HDD (sc1) has too low a baseline to sustain 60 MiB/s across repeated scans, and SSD types cost more.

The data must survive a stop and start, so instance store is out; EBS is needed. Small random I/O at about 2,000 IOPS fits General Purpose SSD (gp3), whose included baseline IOPS cover it at no extra charge; HDD types handle small random I/O poorly and io2 costs more than needed.
